seoTitle: Resize and Reset TradingView Charts to Default
metaDescription: Learn how to resize a TradingView chart by dragging its borders and how to quickly reset the view back to default with a right-click or double-click.
intro: Whether you've zoomed in too far or resized a chart awkwardly, TradingView offers quick shortcuts to fix it. This guide covers resizing charts by dragging borders and resetting the view back to its default state in just a click or two.

steps.heading: Open the chart to adjust
steps.body: Navigate to the chart you want to resize or reset within your TradingView account.

steps.heading: Right-click to open the context menu
steps.body: Right-click anywhere on the chart to bring up the menu with the reset chart view option.

steps.heading: Reset the chart view
steps.body: Select reset chart view to restore the chart to its default visual parameters without losing any data.

steps.heading: Resize by dragging borders
steps.body: Click and drag the sides or edges of the chart border to resize it and focus on specific data segments.

steps.heading: Double-click to revert size
steps.body: Double-click any chart border to instantly return a resized chart back to its original size.

steps.heading: Repeat as needed
steps.body: These shortcuts can be used any time your chart layout gets adjusted in ways you want to undo.

faq.question: How do I reset a TradingView chart to default?
faq.answer: Right-click the chart and select reset chart view to restore the default visual parameters.

faq.question: How can I resize a chart?
faq.answer: Click and drag the sides or edges of the chart border to resize it to your preference.

faq.question: Is there a shortcut to undo a resize?
faq.answer: Yes, double-clicking any chart border instantly returns it to its original size.

faq.question: Will resetting the chart delete my data?
faq.answer: No, resetting the chart view only restores visual settings and doesn't affect your underlying data.

faq.question: Does this work for any asset type?
faq.answer: Yes, these resizing and reset shortcuts work on any chart regardless of the asset being displayed.
